headline: Foundation-model encoders transfer across modalities while stratified benchmarks expose generalization gaps
label: Benchmarking Pretrained Biological Sequence Models
summary: Frozen pLM, folding and RNA encoders are being repurposed with light heads across interaction and variant tasks, while stratified benchmarks test whether gains hold.
synthesis: The dominant thread is reuse of pretrained sequence encoders as general-purpose feature extractors, coupled with scrutiny of what the benchmarks actually measure. Adaptation strategies vary: LoRA-tuned ESM-2 (PALM, TriStageHLA), joint protein-DNA pretraining with domain-aware masking (PDLMs), JEPA objectives for isoform-aware DNA-protein alignment (IsoAlign), zero-shot embedding readout for N-glycosylation (MaskNGly), differential wild-type/mutant logits for SNV effects (MELD), and frozen folding models (Protenix) as antibody screening encoders (FoldAbS). Modality-specific foundation models extend the pattern: structRFM for RNA with new secondary-structure benchmarks, π-SPECFormer pre-trained on 291M mass spectra. The counterweight is evaluation: RPFace pairs a small sequence-only interface predictor with a stratified protein-RNA benchmark exposing structural-benchmark bias, PLMs lose to classical sequence methods for CDR3-based immune-receptor retrieval with germline context confounding results, and the RNA-small molecule survey separates site, preference, and pose tasks. Scale is not uniformly the deciding factor.
